contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you learned Guru Nanak's three core teachings together. Today, let's go deeper into the first one: Naam Japo.

Naam Japo means remembering and meditating on God's name — keeping God present in your mind and heart, not just during formal prayer but throughout everyday life. This doesn't have to mean anything complicated: it can be a quiet moment of gratitude in the morning, a calm breath before starting your day, or simply pausing to notice something beautiful and feeling thankful for it. Try this: take one quiet minute today, sit still, breathe calmly, and think of one thing you're grateful for. That quiet, mindful moment is a simple, real way to practice Naam Japo.
You just practiced a real, simple form of Naam Japo. Tomorrow we'll go deeper into the second teaching: Kirat Karo, honest living.

objectives: Explain Naam Japo as remembering and meditating on God's name in everyday life
Practice one simple, concrete form of Naam Japo (a quiet moment of gratitude)
materialsNeeded: A quiet space for the 1-minute practice
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's overview of all three teachings.
2. Introduce Naam Japo, explicitly connecting it to everyday mindfulness, not just formal prayer.
3. Lead the child through the 1-minute quiet gratitude practice together.
4. Discuss what they noticed or felt during the practice.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's topic: Kirat Karo.
differentiationTips: Struggling: keep the quiet practice very short (30 seconds) and build up gradually over future weeks
Ready for more: ask them to try the same quiet practice at a different time of day and compare how it felt
Keep this deliberately experiential and general rather than tied to a specific memorized prayer text, matching the same caution used in the K-Sikhi Simran lesson earlier this session
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Naam Japo means remembering and meditating on God's name. 2. It can be practiced through a quiet moment of gratitude, not only formal prayer. 3. Answers will vary for what the child felt grateful for during the practice.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Deepens the first of the course's three named core teachings (Naam Japo), matching the 'Day 1 overview, then one deep day per concept' pattern used for other multi-part Sikhi units this session.
